title: t1555: Sanitize cross-references and add intelligence-led approval flow
body:
## Summary

- Wraps all external refs in inline code backticks to prevent GitHub cross-reference leaks
- Adds notification issue creation in private draft-responses repo for GitHub notification-driven approval
- Redesigns approval flow to be intelligence-led (natural language comments) rather than deterministic keyword matching
- Restores `init` command and setup.sh integration

## Problem

When draft-response issues contained `owner/repo#N` patterns in titles or bodies, GitHub created "mentioned this" timeline entries on the external repos — revealing our private draft-responses repo and AI-assisted workflow to external maintainers.

## Fix

All external references are wrapped in inline code backticks (`` `owner/repo#N` ``) which GitHub does not parse for cross-references. Issue titles use plain text descriptions without the `owner/repo#N` pattern.

## Intelligence-Led Approval

Instead of rigid `approved`/`declined` keywords, notification issues now accept natural language:
- "looks good, post it" → approve and post
- Close without comment → decline
- "make it more concise" → re-draft
- Paste custom text → post that instead
- Any other instruction → agent interprets and acts

## Testing

- Created 8 drafts for all contribution-watch items needing reply
- Verified **0 cross-references** leaked to external repos (checked `anomalyco/opencode` and `warpdotdev/Warp` timelines)
- Verified notification issues have clean titles and backtick-wrapped refs in bodies

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.agents/scripts/draft-response-helper.sh` | +167 lines: repo init, notification issues, sanitized refs, approve/reject closing |
| `setup.sh` | Restored `init` call for draft-responses repo creation |

Closes #5475

title: t1556: Wire draft-response approval scanning into contribution-watch routine
body:
## Summary

- Adds `check-approvals` command to `draft-response-helper.sh` — scans open notification issues in the private `draft-responses` repo for user comments, interprets intent via LLM (sonnet tier), and acts accordingly (approve/decline/re-draft/custom/other)
- Wires `check-approvals` into the `contribution-watch-helper.sh` scan cycle so it runs automatically on every hourly scan
- Implements deterministic gate (no LLM cost for issues without new user comments), bot filtering, and role-based compose caps

## Design

### Deterministic layer (shell)
1. Lists open issues with `draft` label in `{user}/draft-responses` repo
2. For each, fetches comments sorted by date
3. Finds user comments newer than the last `github-actions[bot]` comment
4. If found → passes to intelligent layer. If not → skips (zero cost)

### Intelligent layer (LLM)
One sonnet-tier call per actionable comment via `ai-research-helper.sh`. The LLM receives the user's comment, current draft, thread context, and role, then decides:
- **Approve** → posts draft to external repo, closes notification issue with `approved` label
- **Decline** → closes notification issue with `declined` label
- **Re-draft** → composes new draft, updates notification issue body
- **Custom reply** → posts user's text verbatim
- **Other** → interprets and logs extra actions for manual follow-up

### Safety
- Bot comments filtered (`[bot]` suffix + known bot names)
- Role-based compose caps: `participant` = 1 compose total, `author` = unlimited
- Prompt-guard scan on user comments before LLM processing
- No auto-posting without user approval (LLM interprets the comment as approval signal)

## Files changed
- `.agents/scripts/draft-response-helper.sh` — new `check-approvals` command + bot filtering + role caps + LLM interpretation
- `.agents/scripts/contribution-watch-helper.sh` — calls `check-approvals` in scan cycle + updated architecture comment

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] User comments "approved" → reply posted, issue closed
- [x] User comments "declined" → no reply, issue closed
- [x] User comments with custom instructions → LLM interprets and acts
- [x] No LLM calls for issues without new user comments (deterministic gate)
- [x] Bot comments filtered
- [x] Role-based caps enforced
- [x] Runs as part of hourly contribution-watch scan cycle

Closes #5516

Bot comments are ignored and role-based compose limits control who can trigger draft creation.

title: t1556: Fix self-consumption loop guard in check-approvals
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the CRITICAL CodeRabbit finding from PR #5517: the `check-approvals` comment matcher could reconsume the agent's own follow-up comments, causing an infinite LLM call loop on every hourly scan

## Root cause

The `last_handled_comment` cutoff was set to the user's comment timestamp (`latest_user_comment_time`). But actions like `cmd_approve` post follow-up comments (e.g., "Reply posted." via `gh issue close --comment`) under the user's auth — those comments have timestamps AFTER the user's comment. On the next scan, the agent's own follow-up would be newer than the cutoff and picked up as a "new user comment", triggering another LLM interpretation call.

## Fix

Set `last_handled_comment` to the current time (`date -u`) after the action completes, ensuring any agent-posted comments are also covered by the cutoff. This is a single-line semantic change (timestamp source) with no behavioral change to the happy path.

## Verification

- ShellCheck: 0 new violations
- The fix is a timestamp source change — no new code paths, no new dependencies
- The `approve`/`reject` paths close the issue (removing it from the open issues list), so the loop guard primarily protects the `redraft` path where the issue stays open

Closes #5516

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved approval handling logic to prevent the agent from re-processing its own follow-up comments as new user input.

title: fix: add mid-session 429 pool rotation in provider-auth.mjs
body:
## Summary

- **Bug:** `provider-auth.mjs` custom fetch wrapper passed HTTP 429 (rate limit) responses through unhandled. `fetchWithPoolFailover()` existed in `oauth-pool.mjs` but was exported and never called by anything.
- **Fix:** Intercepts 429 responses mid-session, marks the current account as rate-limited, rotates to the next available pool account, and retries the request once with new credentials.
- **Impact:** Users with 2+ OAuth pool accounts now get automatic mid-session rotation when one account hits rate limits, instead of the session failing.

## What was done

- Added `injectPoolToken` import from `oauth-pool.mjs`
- Added `RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS` constant (60 seconds)
- After the `fetch()` call, added 429 interception logic that:
  1. Identifies the current account by matching the access token
  2. Marks it `rate-limited` with a 1-minute cooldown in `oauth-pool.json`
  3. Finds the next available pool account (active, not in cooldown, LRU order)
  4. Refreshes the token via `ensureValidToken()` if needed
  5. Injects the new token into the built-in provider via `injectPoolToken()`
  6. Retries the request once with the new account's credentials
  7. If no alternate account is available, logs and returns the original 429

## How it was tested

- Syntax validation: `node --check provider-auth.mjs` passes
- Logic review: follows the same pattern as the existing (but unused) `fetchWithPoolFailover()` in `oauth-pool.mjs`
- Pool state verified: 2 active Anthropic accounts in `oauth-pool.json` with valid tokens

## Files changed

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs` — added 429 interception and pool rotation logic (+78 lines)

## Key decisions

- Used 1-minute cooldown (matching `RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS` in `oauth-pool.mjs`) rather than parsing `Retry-After` headers — keeps the logic simple and the cooldown short enough for interactive use
- Retry only once per 429 — prevents infinite rotation loops if all accounts are rate-limited
- Reused existing `injectPoolToken()` and `ensureValidToken()` rather than duplicating logic

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved resiliency against temporary rate limits: the system now automatically rotates to alternate accounts and retries requests when a rate limit is encountered, reducing failed requests and interruptions.

title: fix: prevent shellcheck-wrapper infinite recursion on Ubuntu (GH#5526)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the infinite loop during `setup.sh` on Ubuntu 24.04 where the shellcheck-wrapper spawns processes that get killed by the watchdog after 120s timeout, creating an infinite fork loop.

Closes #5526

## Root Cause

When `setup.sh` runs `setup_shellcheck_wrapper` (from `tool-install.sh`), it replaces the real shellcheck binary (e.g., `/usr/bin/shellcheck`) with a copy of the wrapper script and moves the real binary to `/usr/bin/shellcheck.real`. Simultaneously, the PATH shim at `~/.aidevops/bin/shellcheck` is a symlink to the wrapper source at `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/shellcheck-wrapper.sh`.

The `_find_real_shellcheck()` function uses `realpath` for self-detection, but the two wrapper copies resolve to different absolute paths:
- Shim symlink resolves to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/shellcheck-wrapper.sh`
- Binary replacement resolves to `/usr/bin/shellcheck`

Neither copy recognizes the other as "self", so each returns the other as the "real shellcheck", creating mutual infinite recursion. Each level spawns a background watchdog, and after 120s the watchdog kills the child — producing the flood of `WATCHDOG: killing PID` messages reported in the issue.

## Fix (3 defense layers)

1. **Recursion guard** — Environment variable `_SHELLCHECK_WRAPPER_ACTIVE=1` is set on entry. If already set, the wrapper exits immediately with an error instead of searching for the real binary. This is the primary fix that breaks the infinite loop.

2. **Content-based detection** — New `_is_wrapper_copy()` function checks the first 2 bytes of candidate binaries. The real shellcheck is a compiled Haskell binary (ELF/Mach-O magic bytes); wrapper copies start with `#!` (shebang). Any shell script named `shellcheck` is skipped during PATH scanning.

3. **Added `/usr/bin/shellcheck.real` to fast-path** — The existing fast-path only checked `/opt/homebrew/bin/` and `/usr/local/bin/` locations. Ubuntu installs shellcheck at `/usr/bin/`, so the `.real` file there was never found via fast-path, forcing the slow PATH scan where the recursion bug lives.

## Testing

- Verified wrapper still finds and runs real shellcheck: `shellcheck-wrapper.sh --version` → success
- Verified recursion guard blocks re-entry: `_SHELLCHECK_WRAPPER_ACTIVE=1 shellcheck-wrapper.sh --version` → error + exit 1
- Simulated the Ubuntu scenario (wrapper copy on PATH + symlink shim) → correctly finds `.real` binary, no recursion
- Simulated edge case (no `.real` file, wrapper copies on PATH) → correctly skips copies, finds real binary on system PATH
- ShellCheck clean: zero violations

title: GH#5530: fix: kill entire process group on sandbox timeout
body:
## Summary

- Replaces `timeout_sec` calls in `sandbox_run` with `_sandbox_exec_with_pgkill`, a new inline function that runs the worker in a new process group via `setsid` and kills the entire group on timeout
- Fixes workers running 7-9h past the 1h timeout (GH#5530): `timeout` only killed the direct child; grandchildren (MCP servers, node workers) survived and kept the bash wrapper alive indefinitely
- SIGTERM sent to process group first, SIGKILL after 0.5s grace period for any survivors

## Root cause

Process tree when dispatching a worker:
```
bash sandbox-exec-helper.sh
  └── timeout 3600
        └── env -i ... opencode run   ← timeout kills this
              ├── node mcp-server     ← survives (not a direct child of timeout)
              └── node mcp-server     ← survives
```
The orphaned grandchildren kept the bash wrapper alive via implicit `wait`.

## Fix

`_sandbox_exec_with_pgkill` uses `setsid` to start the command in a new process group, then polls with `kill -0` and kills the entire group (`kill -- -PGID`) when the deadline expires. stdout/stderr are passed as file paths so redirection applies to the backgrounded child, not the polling loop.

## Verification

Tested inline with a simulated worker that spawns 2 child processes:
- 3 processes in group before timeout kill
- 0 processes remaining after kill
- Exit code 124 returned correctly
- Normal completion path: stdout captured, exit code propagated correctly (tested with exit 42)

ShellCheck: zero new violations (only pre-existing SC1091 info on sourced file).

Closes #5530

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Improved sandbox execution so spawned tasks run in isolated process groups and are reliably terminated on timeout or exit.
  * Standardized timeout handling and output capture, ensuring timeouts are reported consistently and stdout/stderr are preserved for diagnostics.

title: GH#5530: fix: kill process group in timeout_sec() macOS fallback
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the macOS fallback in `timeout_sec()` (`shared-constants.sh`) to kill the entire process group instead of just the direct child PID
- Completes the fix for GH#5530 — the `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` portion was already merged via PR #5531, this applies the remaining `shared-constants.sh` portion that was in PR #5532 (closed due to merge conflicts)

## Root Cause

The macOS fallback path in `timeout_sec()` used `kill "$cmd_pid"` which only kills the direct child. When the timed-out command spawns its own children (MCP servers, node workers), those grandchildren survive and keep the parent wrapper alive indefinitely — workers ran 7-9h past the 1h timeout.

## Fix

- Use `set -m` to put the background job in its own process group (PGID == child PID)
- Use `kill -- -PGID` to send SIGTERM/SIGKILL to the entire process group
- This matches the approach already applied to `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` in PR #5531

## Verification

- ShellCheck: zero violations on `shared-constants.sh`
- Diff matches exactly what PR #5532 proposed for this file

Closes #5530

title: fix: pool injection idle status + headless dispatch timing race
body:
Two bugs identified from user report (Rob S.) — headless /runners failing while interactive sessions work.

## Bug 1 — `injectPoolToken` skips `idle` accounts

`oauth-pool.mjs:1310` filtered `status === "active"` only. After `reset-cooldowns` sets accounts to `"idle"`, injection returned `false` and nothing was written to `auth.json`. `injectOpenAIPoolToken` already accepted `active || idle` correctly — this aligns Anthropic to match.

## Bug 2 — `initPoolAuth` timing race in headless mode

`initPoolAuth` was called in the `AidevopsPlugin()` factory body — before OpenCode finished its own provider initialisation. In headless `opencode run`, the first API call fires before the factory returns, so `client.auth.set()` either hadn't run or its write wasn't picked up by the provider layer yet. Interactive TUI works because human latency absorbs the gap.

Fix: move `initPoolAuth` into the `config` hook, which OpenCode calls as part of its own initialisation sequence before any provider calls.

## Root cause of Rob's symptom
- `anthropic` entry in auth.json: VALID (written by a previous interactive session)
- `anthropic-pool` entry: EXPIRED (stale from pool provider UI flow)
- Headless dispatch was hitting the expired entry because injection hadn't run yet

title: fix: inject OAuth tokens via env vars — works on all OpenCode versions
body:
## Problem

OpenCode 1.3.0+ uses bundled `@ai-sdk/anthropic` which reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `process.env`, ignoring `auth.json` entirely. Our `client.auth.set()` injection worked on <=1.2.27 but was invisible to the bundled SDK — causing `AI_LoadAPIKeyError` for all OAuth users on 1.3.0.

## Fix

Set `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and `OPENAI_API_KEY`) with the OAuth access token at every injection point. The Anthropic API accepts OAuth access tokens in the same `x-api-key` header as API keys.

Injection points updated:
- `injectPoolToken` (startup)
- `injectOpenAIPoolToken` (startup)
- Mid-session account add (both providers)
- 429 rotation (calls inject functions which now update env var)

`client.auth.set()` kept for backward compat with <=1.2.27 but demoted to best-effort.

## Testing

Sandbox headless run on OpenCode 1.3.0:
- Before: `AI_LoadAPIKeyError: Anthropic API key is missing`
- After: Model responds successfully (`hello`)

## Also in this PR

- Lifts the 1.2.27 version pin (no longer needed)
- Restores OpenCode in auto-upgrade list
- Updates auth-troubleshooting.md with env var injection details

body:
## Summary

Addresses all 3 findings from the Gemini code review on PR #5548 (`.agents/scripts/opencode-sandbox-helper.sh`).

## Findings Fixed

### HIGH (×2) — `nullglob` for glob loops under `set -e`

**Problem**: With `set -e` active, `for dir in "${SANDBOX_ROOT}"/*/;` exits the script with an error when no sandbox directories exist — the glob literal is passed as a non-existent path.

**Fix**: Wrap both affected loops (`_latest_sandbox` line 81 and `cmd_list` line 202) with `shopt -s nullglob` / `shopt -u nullglob`. This causes the glob to expand to nothing when no directories match, so the loop body is simply skipped. The redundant `[[ ! -d "$dir" ]] && continue` guard is removed as it becomes unnecessary.

### MEDIUM (×1) — Replace `shift 2>/dev/null || true` with explicit guard

**Problem**: `shift 2>/dev/null || true` silences errors to handle the case where `$#` is 0 under `set -e`. This suppresses stderr and can mask real issues.

**Fix**: Replace with the explicit conditional `if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then shift; fi` — same semantics, no error suppression.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-sandbox-helper.sh` — clean (only pre-existing SC1091 info about external file sourcing)
- Blast radius: 1 file, 5 insertions / 3 deletions

title: fix: improve contributions dedup and fix extra newline in profile-readme-helper
body:
## Summary

Addresses medium-severity Gemini review feedback from PR #5523 on `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh`.

Closes #5562

## Changes

### 1. Fix incomplete and inefficient deduplication in `_generate_contributions()`

**Problem**: The old grep-based dedup (`grep -qF "/${repo_name})"`) had three issues:
- **O(N*M) performance**: grepped the entire accumulated markdown string for every repos.json entry
- **Incomplete coverage**: only deduped repos.json entries against forks, not within forks or within repos.json entries themselves
- **Fragile matching**: partial name matches could cause false positives (e.g., `app` matching `webapp`)

**Fix**: Introduced a newline-delimited `seen_repos` tracking variable with `grep -qxF` (exact whole-line match) that deduplicates across ALL sources — within forks, within repos.json, and across both. Bash 3.2 compatible (no associative arrays).

### 2. Fix extra blank line in contributions block output

**Problem**: `printf "%s\n", block` in the awk script added a newline to `CONTRIBS_BLOCK`, which already ends with a trailing newline from `_generate_contributions()`. This produced a double blank line before `<!-- CONTRIBUTIONS-END -->`.

**Fix**: Changed to `printf "%s", block` to preserve the existing trailing newline without adding a second one.

## Verification

- ShellCheck: zero violations
- Existing boundary test (`test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`): PASS (1/1)
- Both findings verified against current code before fixing
- Gemini's suggested associative array approach was rejected as bash 4.0+ only (violates project's bash 3.2 compatibility requirement)

title: fix: add --privacy-filter flag to session-checkpoint-helper.sh save

## Summary

- Adds `--privacy-filter` flag to the `save` command in `session-checkpoint-helper.sh`
- When the flag is set, checkpoint content is written to a temp file first, scanned by `privacy-filter-helper.sh scan`, and only moved to the final location if no secrets are detected
- If secrets are detected, the temp file is deleted and the save fails with exit code 1, preventing credential leakage into checkpoint files
- Updates the header comment/usage docs to document the new flag

## Root Cause (from GH#5546)

Session checkpoints lacked automated privacy filtering. An agent could copy credential values into a `--note` field or the checkpoint could capture sensitive git/env state, writing it to disk without any scan.

## Behaviour

```bash
# Without flag — saves unconditionally (existing behaviour preserved)
session-checkpoint-helper.sh save --task t001 --note "some context"

# With flag — scans first, fails if secrets detected
session-checkpoint-helper.sh save --task t001 --note "some context" --privacy-filter
# Exit 0: checkpoint saved
# Exit 1: secrets detected, save aborted, findings printed to stderr
```

## Testing

- `shellcheck` passes (zero new violations; pre-existing SC1091 info notice unchanged)
- Smoke tested: save without flag works, save with flag on clean content passes, save with flag on content containing home directory paths fails with exit 1 and prints findings

Prevents `invalid x-api-key` / `Invalid authentication credentials` errors by keeping OAuth tokens fresh before they expire.

## Three refresh layers

| Layer | Trigger | How |
|-------|---------|-----|
| **Scheduled** | Every 30 min (launchd/cron) | `sh.aidevops.token-refresh` plist, RunAtLoad=true |
| **Session startup** | Every new OpenCode/Claude session | Background refresh in `aidevops-update-check.sh` |
| **On rotate** | When switching accounts | Auto-refresh in `cmd_rotate` (from v3.1.84) |

- `setup.sh`: installs/updates the launchd plist (macOS) or cron entry (Linux)

## Root cause of the bug

Tokens expire after ~8 hours. If a session runs longer than that, or the machine sleeps and wakes after expiry, the next API call fails with `invalid x-api-key`. Nothing was refreshing tokens proactively.

title: fix: trigger pool rotation on 401/403 auth errors, not just 429
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root cause of mid-session `invalid x-api-key` / `Invalid authentication credentials` errors by handling 401/403 in the pool failover, not just 429.

## Behaviour change

| Status | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| **429** (rate limit) | Rotate to next account, retry | Same (unchanged) |
| **401/403** (auth error) | Session dies | Refresh current token → retry. If refresh fails → rotate to next account → retry |

## How it works

On 401/403, `fetchWithPoolFailover()` now:

1. Attempts to refresh the current account's token via `ensureValidToken()` with `expires: 0` (forces refresh)
2. If refresh succeeds: updates `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` env var and retries the request — no rotation needed
3. If refresh fails: marks the account as `auth-error` with a 5-minute cooldown, rotates to the next available account, and retries once

This means a token expiring mid-session is now self-healing — the user never sees the error.

## Testing

- Cannot trigger a real 401 without waiting for token expiry, but the code path is identical to the existing 429 path (which is battle-tested) with the addition of the refresh-first step
- The `ensureValidToken()` function is already used by `injectPoolToken()` on every session start — proven working

title: t1557: Fix profile README recovery from diverged history and missing markers
body:
## Summary

- Fix profile-readme-helper.sh to recover when a user's GitHub profile repo is deleted and recreated (diverged git history)
- Inject aidevops stat markers into existing READMEs instead of overwriting user content
- Make setup.sh always run `init` (idempotent) to catch diverged/missing-marker states on every update

Closes #5610

## What was done

**Problem:** When a user deletes and recreates their `username/username` GitHub profile repo, the local clone has diverged history. The hourly update job commits stats locally but `git push` fails silently — the profile page on GitHub shows the default template indefinitely. Running `aidevops update` or `setup.sh` doesn't fix it because the local README still has markers, so the init guard returns early.

Additionally, if a user writes their own README without aidevops markers, `cmd_update` would error out and `cmd_init` would overwrite the entire file.

**Fix (3 files, 3 changes):**

1. **`profile-readme-helper.sh`** — 4 changes:
   - New `_inject_markers_into_readme()`: appends `STATS-START/END`, `CONTRIBUTIONS-START/END`, and `UPDATED-START/END` marker blocks to the end of an existing README without overwriting any user content
   - New `_recover_diverged_profile()`: backs up the local clone, re-clones from remote, injects markers, commits, pushes, and cleans up the backup
   - `cmd_init` guard: now runs `git fetch` + `merge-base` check to detect diverged history even when local README has markers; calls `_recover_diverged_profile` on divergence
   - `cmd_update` push failure: instead of silently returning, attempts diverged history recovery and re-runs the update cycle
   - `_resolve_profile_repo` fallback: no longer requires `<!-- STATS-START -->` markers to recognize the profile repo — `cmd_init`/`cmd_update` will inject them

2. **`setup.sh`**: Always runs `profile-readme-helper.sh init` instead of checking local markers and skipping. `cmd_init` is idempotent — returns early when everything is fine, but now catches diverged/missing-marker states.

3. **`test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`**: 2 new tests:
   - `inject markers into README without markers`: creates a user-authored README, runs update, verifies markers were injected and original content preserved
   - `recover from diverged git history`: simulates repo deletion/recreation, runs update, verifies markers exist and push works after recovery

## How it was tested

- All 3 tests pass (1 existing + 2 new)
- ShellCheck clean on all modified files
- Bash 3.2 compatible (no associative arrays, no bash 4.0+ features)

## Files changed

- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh` — core fix: marker injection, diverged history recovery, updated init/update/resolve flows
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` — 2 new test cases
- `setup.sh` — simplified profile README check to always run init

title: fix: handle 401/403 (server-side token revocation) in OAuth pool with auto-refresh
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: Anthropic revokes OAuth access tokens server-side before the local expiry timestamp (tokens claim 8h validity but are rejected after ~1-2h idle). Three users independently hit `invalid x-api-key` on session start after a break.
- **provider-auth.mjs**: Added 401/403 handler — force-refreshes the current account's token first, then rotates to next pool account if refresh fails (same retry-once pattern as existing 429 handler)
- **oauth-pool.mjs `ensureValidToken()`**: Added proactive refresh when token has used >50% of its claimed lifetime, preventing the gap between local expiry and server-side revocation. Graceful fallback: if proactive refresh fails, the existing token is still returned

## What was broken

1. `ensureValidToken()` only checked `account.expires > Date.now()` — if the local timestamp said "valid", it returned the stale token without testing it against the API
2. `provider-auth.mjs` fetch wrapper handled 429 (rate limit) with rotation, but did NOT handle 401/403 (invalid token) — the error propagated straight to the user
3. `fetchWithPoolFailover()` in oauth-pool.mjs DID handle 401/403, but was never called from provider-auth.mjs

## Testing

- Verified both refresh tokens still work against Anthropic's token endpoint
- Deployed to `~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/` for immediate testing
- Next session start will exercise the proactive refresh path

title: feat: Bridge Google OAuth pool tokens to OpenCode's Google provider (issue #5622)
body:
## Summary

- Add `google-proxy.mjs` — a lightweight HTTP proxy on `localhost:32124` that translates between `@ai-sdk/google`'s `x-goog-api-key` auth and our OAuth pool's Bearer token auth
- Integrate proxy startup into the plugin lifecycle (`index.mjs` Phase 9) — starts automatically when Google pool accounts exist
- Discover models from the API on startup and register them in `opencode.json` so they appear in the `Ctrl+T` model picker

## Technical Details

Google's Generative AI API uses two incompatible auth mechanisms:

| Method | Header | Used by |
|--------|--------|---------|
| API Key | `x-goog-api-key: <key>` | `@ai-sdk/google` (OpenCode's built-in) |
| OAuth Bearer | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | Gemini CLI, our pool |

The proxy bridges this gap by:
1. Accepting requests from `@ai-sdk/google` (which sends `x-goog-api-key`)
2. Stripping `x-goog-api-key`, adding `Authorization: Bearer <pool-token>`
3. Forwarding to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`
4. Piping responses back (including SSE streams for `streamGenerateContent`)

Follows the proven `cursor-proxy.mjs` pattern but significantly simpler — HTTP-to-HTTP header rewriting only (~540 lines vs ~330 for cursor which needs gRPC/protobuf).

## Key Features

- **Auth translation**: strips `x-goog-api-key`, adds `Authorization: Bearer`
- **Model discovery**: `GET /v1beta/models` on startup, filters for `generateContent`-capable models
- **Pool rotation**: rotates to next account on 429 (same as Anthropic/OpenAI/Cursor)
- **SSE streaming**: pipes `response.body` directly for `streamGenerateContent`
- **Isolation**: proxy failure never affects Anthropic/OpenAI/Cursor providers
- **Fixed port**: 32124 (configurable via `GOOGLE_PROXY_PORT` env var)

## Files Changed

- **New**: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/google-proxy.mjs` — the proxy implementation
- **Modified**: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` — import, Phase 9 startup, config hook model registration

Closes #5622

title: GH#5628: feat: add periodic complexity scanning to pulse for continuous improvement
body:
## Summary

- Add weekly complexity scan to `pulse-wrapper.sh` that creates `simplification-debt` issues for files with many complex functions (>= 5 functions exceeding 100 lines)
- Move CI complexity thresholds from hardcoded values to `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` for ratcheting after simplification PRs merge
- Document the automated scan + CI ratchet workflow in `code-simplifier.md`

## Problem

The complexity reduction pipeline was fully built (CI gate, `/code-simplifier` command, pulse dispatch for `simplification-debt`, human gate workflow) but had **no periodic trigger** — nobody invoked `/code-simplifier`, so zero `simplification-debt` issues were being created automatically. The CI threshold (420) was static and already exceeded (421 violations).

## Solution

### 1. Weekly complexity scan in pulse-wrapper

`run_weekly_complexity_scan()` runs during the pulse pre-flight phase (after cleanup, before prefetch). It:

1. Checks a timestamp file to ensure it runs at most once per `COMPLEXITY_SCAN_INTERVAL` (default 7 days)
2. Runs the same awk-based function complexity check used by CI
3. Groups violations by file and filters to files with >= `COMPLEXITY_FILE_VIOLATION_THRESHOLD` (default 5) violations
4. Deduplicates against existing open `simplification-debt` issues for the same file
5. Creates issues with `simplification-debt` + `needs-maintainer-review` labels, assigned to the repo maintainer

### 2. CI threshold ratchet

CI now reads thresholds from `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` instead of hardcoding them. After each batch of simplification PRs merges, lowering the values in this file prevents regression.

### 3. Documentation

Updated `code-simplifier.md` to document both input paths (automated weekly scan + manual `/code-simplifier`) and the CI ratchet workflow.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -S error pulse-wrapper.sh` — zero violations
- `bash -n pulse-wrapper.sh` — syntax OK
- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` — YAML valid
- All existing pulse-wrapper tests pass (18/18 in worker-detection, terminal-blockers, ci-failure-prefetch)
- Config file validated (3 key=value pairs, all numeric)

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` | Add `run_weekly_complexity_scan()` + config vars + call in `main()` |
| `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` | Read thresholds from config file |
| `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` | New: threshold values for CI gates |
| `.agents/tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` | Document automated scan + ratchet |

Closes #5628

title: feat: weekly complexity scan pulse trigger with ratchetable CI thresholds (GH#5628)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `run_weekly_complexity_scan()` to `pulse-wrapper.sh`: runs the same awk-based function complexity check as CI, creates `simplification-debt` issues for files with 5+ functions >100 lines, at most once per 7 days
- Adds `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf`: ratchetable thresholds for CI gates — lower after each batch of simplification PRs merges
- Updates `code-quality.yml` to read thresholds from the config file instead of hardcoded values
- Updates `code-simplifier.md` to document the automated weekly scan path and CI threshold ratchet workflow

## CodeRabbit fixes (from PR #5630 review)

Three bugs fixed that were flagged on the original PR:

**Bug 1 (Major): Multiline `details` in `scan_results` broke IFS parser**
`details=$(echo "$result" | head -10)` stored multiline content in the pipe-delimited `scan_results` string, causing the downstream `while IFS='|' read -r file_path violation_count details` loop to misalign fields. Fixed by removing `details` from `scan_results` entirely — `scan_results` now stores only `file|count`, and details are recomputed inside the issue-creation loop.

**Bug 2 (Major): Basename dedup collapsed different files with same name**
`basename_file=$(basename "$file_path")` meant `scripts/setup.sh` and `tests/setup.sh` would match the same existing issue. Also `--limit 50` could miss open matches, and the `gh issue list` call was inside the per-file loop (unnecessary API traffic). Fixed: use `issue_key="$file_path"` (full repo-relative path), fetch `existing_issues` once before the loop with `--limit 200`, match on both title and body.

**Bug 3 (Minor): `grep|cut` pipelines in `code-quality.yml` could abort under `errexit`**
`val=$(grep '^KEY=' file | cut -d= -f2)` exits non-zero when the key is missing, which aborts the step under GitHub Actions' default `errexit`. Fixed by appending `|| true` to all three pipelines (FUNCTION_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD, NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD, FILE_SIZE_THRESHOLD).

## Closes

Closes #5628

title: t1557: Detect default GitHub template README and replace with rich profile
body:
## Summary

- Detect the default GitHub profile template README and replace it with the full rich profile (name, bio, badges, stats) instead of just appending markers
- Follow-up to #5611 which fixed diverged history recovery but left the default template content in place

Closes #5610

## What was done

**Problem:** After the v3.1.87 fix (#5611), the profile-readme-helper correctly injects markers into existing READMEs. But when the README is the default GitHub template ("Hi there" + commented-out suggestions), it only appends markers to the bottom — leaving the useless template content at the top. The profile ends up with stats but no name, bio, or language badges.

**Fix:** Added `_is_default_github_template()` detection and updated all code paths (cmd_init, cmd_update, _recover_diverged_profile) to generate the full rich README when the default template is detected, instead of just injecting markers.

**Detection criteria:**
- "Hi there" heading + "is a special repository" comment block (the distinctive GitHub default)
- Or: README with 3 or fewer lines and no existing markers (minimal default like `# username`)

## Files changed

- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh` — new `_is_default_github_template()` function, updated 3 code paths
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` — 1 new test for default template replacement

title: GH#5650: Fix worker-watchdog to detect workers stalled by mid-session provider backoff
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root cause of 4 workers running 11+ hours with 0 commits after the anthropic provider hit `auth_error` at 04:58 and was backed off for 1 hour. The watchdog had no visibility into the headless-runtime `provider_backoff` table, so it couldn't detect that workers were alive but permanently stalled.

## Root Cause

Two gaps:
1. **No backoff check** — `worker-watchdog.sh` never consulted the `headless-runtime/state.db` `provider_backoff` table. Workers whose provider was backed off continued running indefinitely.
2. **Struggle ratio threshold too high** — The primary thrash check requires ratio > 30 with `flag == "thrashing"`. Workers with ratio 14 at 7+ hours with 0 commits (clearly stuck) were missed.

## Changes

### `worker-watchdog.sh`
- **`extract_provider_from_cmd()`** — extracts provider name from `--model` flag (e.g., `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` → `anthropic`)
- **`check_provider_backoff()`** — queries `provider_backoff` table in headless-runtime `state.db`; detects active backoff entries where `retry_after` is in the future (or NULL = indefinite). Skips workers in 5-minute grace period.
- **Check 1 in `cmd_check()`** — backoff check runs before all other checks and **bypasses the transcript gate** (provider won't respond regardless of what the transcript says)
- **Kill reason `backoff`** → `status:available` (re-queue immediately, not blocked)
- **Time-weighted thrash check** — elapsed >= 7h AND commits == 0 AND ratio >= 10 triggers kill even if ratio < 30 primary threshold. Catches the ratio-14 workers from the incident.
- **New config vars**: `WORKER_THRASH_RATIO_THRESHOLD` (default: 10), `WORKER_THRASH_RATIO_ELAPSED` (default: 25200s = 7h)
- `HEADLESS_RUNTIME_DB` is no longer `readonly` (must be overridable by env var and tests)
- Updated `--status` output and `--help` to document new signals

### `tests/test-worker-stall-diagnosis.sh`
- 9 new tests: `extract_provider_from_cmd` (3), `check_provider_backoff` (3), backoff kill labels (1), time-weighted thrash (2)
- All 20 tests pass, 0 failures

## Verification


title: fix: discover shell scripts via git ls-files in quality sweep (GH#5663)
body:
## Summary

- Replace `find` with `git ls-files '*.sh'` in `_quality_sweep_for_repo` ShellCheck section to avoid false findings on untracked/deleted files
- Add fallback to `find` for non-git directories (should not occur for pulse repos but handles edge cases)
- Resolve relative paths returned by `git ls-files` to absolute paths before passing to ShellCheck
- Add file-existence guard: skip tracked-but-deleted files (index vs working tree mismatch) with a log entry

## Problem

`find` scans the filesystem and returns paths not tracked by git — deleted scripts still on disk, stale worktree paths, build artifacts. This caused false ShellCheck findings and spurious quality-debt issues (evidence: GH#650 in a managed repo reported SC2086 on two files that `git ls-files` showed did not exist).

## Changes

`stats-functions.sh` lines ~1251-1287 (ShellCheck section of `_quality_sweep_for_repo`):

```bash
# Before
sh_files=$(find "$repo_path" -name "*.sh" ... | head -100)

# After
if git -C "$repo_path" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    sh_files=$(git -C "$repo_path" ls-files '*.sh' 2>/dev/null | head -100)
else
    sh_files=$(find "$repo_path" -name "*.sh" ... | head -100)  # fallback
fi
# + relative→absolute path resolution
# + [[ ! -f "$shfile" ]] guard before ShellCheck invocation
```

## Verification

- ShellCheck on modified file: **0 violations** (unchanged from baseline)
- 1 file changed, 20 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

Closes #5663

title: fix: verify stored PIDs are alive before reporting duplicate in dispatch-dedup-helper
body:
## Summary

Fixes `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` `is_duplicate()` to verify stored PIDs are alive before returning exit 0 (duplicate). Dead PIDs from previous sessions were causing the pulse to skip valid, unworked issues.

## Root cause

The supervisor DB check queried tasks with `status IN ('running', 'dispatched', 'evaluating')` and returned DUPLICATE without verifying the worker process was still running. When a worker dies without updating the DB (SIGKILL, power loss, OOM), the stale record blocks future dispatch indefinitely.

## Fix

When a DB match is found, the fix:
1. Reads the PID from `$SUPERVISOR_DIR/pids/${task_id}.pid`
2. Uses `kill -0 $pid` to check liveness (zero-signal, no side effects)
3. If dead: resets DB status to `failed` with a diagnostic error message, returns exit 1 (safe to dispatch)
4. If alive: returns exit 0 (genuine duplicate — existing behaviour preserved)
5. If no PID file: treats as stale, resets DB status to `failed`, returns exit 1

## Evidence from issue

- Issue #649 (gratis-ai-agent): dedup reported PID 728337 running, `ps -p 728337` showed NOT RUNNING
- Issue #650 (gratis-ai-agent): dedup reported PID 886890 running, `ps -p 886890` showed NOT RUNNING
- Workaround required unique session key suffix to bypass stale check

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero violations
- Logic: `kill -0` is POSIX-portable, zero-signal (no side effects), works on macOS and Linux
- Stale entry cleanup: DB UPDATE is wrapped in `|| true` so sqlite3 failures don't abort the check

Closes #5662

title: GH#5662: Fix dispatch-dedup-helper.sh dead PID false duplicates
body:
## Summary

- Add `kill -0` PID liveness checks in `list_running_keys()` and `is_duplicate()` to skip dead/zombie PIDs before reporting DUPLICATE
- Add staleness threshold (`DEDUP_DB_STALENESS_SECONDS`, default 7200s) to supervisor DB queries so stale entries from crashed workers don't block new dispatch
- Add test suite (`test-dispatch-dedup-dead-pid.sh`) verifying dead PIDs are correctly ignored

## Problem

`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-duplicate` returned exit 0 (duplicate) for issues where the referenced PID was no longer running. This caused the pulse to skip dispatch for valid, unworked issues, leaving worker slots idle.

Evidence from issue: PID 728337 and PID 886890 were reported as running by dedup, but `ps -p` showed NOT RUNNING.

## Root Cause

Two paths could report false duplicates:

1. **Process-based check**: `pgrep -f` can return PIDs for zombie processes or processes about to exit. The existing `ps -p` check catches some cases but not all (race conditions, zombies).
2. **Supervisor DB check**: Tasks stuck in `running`/`dispatched`/`evaluating` status from dead workers persisted indefinitely with no staleness guard.

## Fix

1. Added `kill -0 $pid` verification in `list_running_keys()` before processing each PID — filters out zombies and dead processes early
2. Added `kill -0 $match_pid` double-check in `is_duplicate()` before returning DUPLICATE — catches PIDs that died between listing and matching
3. Added `updated_at` staleness filter to all supervisor DB queries — entries older than `DEDUP_DB_STALENESS_SECONDS` (default 2h, matching max worker runtime) are ignored

## Testing

- New: `test-dispatch-dedup-dead-pid.sh` — 3 tests verifying dead PID handling
- Existing: `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh` — 3 tests pass (no regression)
- ShellCheck: clean

Closes #5662

title: GH#5668: fix(quality-feedback): filter human APPROVED merge/CI-status comments
body:
## Summary

Fixes two root causes that caused the pulse supervisor's merge approval comment to be filed as a quality-debt issue (incident: issue #5668, PR #5637).

- **Root cause 1**: Human `APPROVED` reviews bypassed all positive-review filters. The `select()` block had `elif $reviewer == "human" then true` which unconditionally passed all human reviews regardless of content. Fix: human `APPROVED` reviews now require `$actionable` content (same as bots). `CHANGES_REQUESTED` reviews remain always-actionable via a new first branch.

- **Root cause 2**: Merge/CI-status comments (e.g. `"Pulse supervisor: all CI checks green, review-bot-gate PASS, CodeRabbit approved. Merging."`) were not matched by any existing filter. The `$approval_only` pattern requires the entire body to be a short approval phrase — these operational messages are not. title: GH#5677: Fix memory-helper.sh recall FTS5 query failure
body:
## Summary

- Fix `.param set` double-quote expansion in heredoc that caused all `memory-helper.sh recall` queries to fail with `fts5: syntax error near ""`
- Convert shared (global DB) search from direct string interpolation to parameterized `.param set` binding for consistency and SQL injection safety

## Root Cause

In `recall.sh` line 262, `.param set :query "$escaped_query"` used double quotes inside a heredoc (`<<EOF`). When `$escaped_query` contained FTS5-quoted tokens like `"bottled"`, the heredoc expansion consumed the double quotes — sqlite3 received `.param set :query bottled` (no quotes) or an empty string, causing the FTS5 syntax error.

## Fix

Changed to single quotes: `.param set :query '${escaped_query}'`. Single quotes inside a heredoc are literal characters (not shell quoting), so sqlite3 receives the full FTS5 query string with its double-quoted tokens intact.

## Verification

Tested with sqlite3 FTS5:
- Single-word query `"bottled"` (was failing with syntax error) — now returns correct result
- Multi-word query `"custom" "water"` — returns correct result
- Old double-quote pattern confirmed to reproduce the exact error from the issue

ShellCheck: zero violations.

Closes #5677

title: GH#5677: Preserve apostrophes in FTS5 .param set quoting
body:
## Summary

- Replace lossy apostrophe-stripping workaround with proper SQL literal escaping for sqlite3's `.param set` dot-command
- Queries like `O'Reilly` now preserve the apostrophe instead of being split into `O Reilly`
- Uses SQL single-quoted literal wrapped in double-quoted dot-command argument per sqlite3 CLI docs

## Problem

PR #5678 merged with a workaround that stripped apostrophes from queries before tokenization (`O'Reilly` → `O Reilly`). While functionally correct for FTS5 matching (the tokenizer splits on apostrophes anyway), this was lossy and didn't address the root cause identified by CodeRabbit and Gemini reviewers.

**Root cause**: sqlite3's dot-command parser does NOT support `''` escaping inside single-quoted arguments. The dot-command parser is separate from the SQL parser. So `.param set :query '"O''Reilly"'` breaks at the first embedded `'`.

## Fix

Build the `.param set` value as an SQL single-quoted literal, then escape it for the dot-command's double-quoted argument context:

```
.param set :query "'\"O''Reilly\" \"guide\"'"
```

- Outer `"..."`: dot-command argument boundary (supports `\"` escaping)
- Inner `'...'`: SQL text literal delimiters
- `''`: SQL-escaped apostrophe (evaluated by SQL parser, not dot-command parser)
- `\"`: dot-command-escaped double quote (preserves FTS5 token quoting)

Uses `sed` for the escaping pipeline to avoid bash quoting conflicts between parameter expansion and heredoc contexts.

## Verification

All 10 test cases pass:
- Simple multi-word, single word, hyphenated tokens
- **O'Reilly**, **can't**, **it's O'Reilly's book** (apostrophe cases)
- Backslash stripping, JSON output mode
- ShellCheck: zero violations

## Review Comments Addressed

Addresses all 5 unresolved review comments from PR #5678:
1. **CodeRabbit (line 262)**: `.param set` quoting — now uses SQL literal in double-quoted dot-command arg
2. **CodeRabbit (line 332)**: shared-mode filter propagation — already fixed in #5678, preserved
3. **Gemini critical (line 262)**: FTS5 syntax correctness — preserved and improved
4. **Gemini security-high (line 319)**: parameterized binding for shared query — preserved
5. **Gemini security-high (line 332)**: `:query` parameter vs interpolation — preserved

Closes #5677

title: GH#5683: Fix recall.sh apostrophe escaping and shared mode filter bypass
body:
## Summary

- Fix `.param set` double-quote escaping so FTS5 queries with apostrophes (e.g., `O'Reilly guide`) work correctly
- Add missing `--auto-only`/`--manual-only` and `--entity` filters to `--shared` mode global DB query
- Switch shared query from direct string interpolation to parameterized `.param set` binding

## Root Cause

Two bugs identified by CodeRabbit review on PR #5678 (post-merge findings):

### 1. Apostrophe/single-quote in queries breaks `.param set`

`.param set :query "$escaped_query"` in a heredoc (`<<EOF`) — the FTS5 token double quotes (`"word"`) were consumed by the heredoc's double-quote expansion, leaving sqlite3 with malformed input. For queries containing apostrophes like `O'Reilly`, this produced FTS5 syntax errors.

**Fix:** Escape backslashes and double quotes in `tokenised_query` before interpolation. sqlite3 `.param set` with a double-quoted VALUE treats apostrophes as literal characters, so `O'Reilly` passes through safely.

### 2. `--shared` mode bypassed filters

The shared/global DB query only applied `$extra_filters` but omitted:
- `$auto_join_filter` (`--auto-only` / `--manual-only`)
- `$entity_fts_join` and `$entity_fts_where` (`--entity` filtering)
- Used direct string interpolation (`'$escaped_query'`) instead of `.param set` binding

**Fix:** Added all missing filter variables and switched to parameterized binding, consistent with the namespace query.

## Verification

- `O'Reilly guide` (apostrophe) — previously failed, now returns correct result

## Summary

title: Fix worktree cleanup: grace period, open PR, and zero-commit safety checks
body:
## Summary

Fixes `cmd_clean()` in `worktree-helper.sh` to prevent deletion of in-progress dirty worktrees when called with `--force-merged` (as the pulse does).

## Root Cause

A branch with 0 commits ahead of the default branch is treated as merged by `git branch --merged` because it shares the same HEAD. A freshly created worktree with uncommitted work and no commits yet would be incorrectly flagged as merged and deleted when `--force-merged` is set.

## Three Safety Checks Added

Both the **detection pass** (what to show) and the **removal pass** (what to delete) now enforce:

### A. Grace Period (`WORKTREE_CLEAN_GRACE_HOURS`, default 4h)
Worktrees younger than the grace period are skipped even with `--force-merged`. Uses directory mtime as a proxy for creation time. Configurable via env var.

### B. Open PR Check
If the branch has an open PR (pre-fetched as `open_pr_branches` list — one API call, not N), the worktree is active work in progress and is skipped regardless of flags.

### C. Zero-Commit + Dirty Check
A branch with 0 commits ahead of default AND uncommitted files is in-progress, not truly merged. This is the specific bug: `git branch --merged` treats 0-commit branches as merged.

## New Helper Functions

All Bash 3.2 compatible, ShellCheck clean (zero new violations):

- `worktree_is_in_grace_period()` — mtime-based age check (macOS `stat -f %m` + Linux `stat -c %Y`)
- `branch_has_open_pr()` — per-branch gh CLI check (for external callers)
- `branch_has_zero_commits_ahead()` — `git rev-list --count` check

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Dirty worktree with 0 commits ahead + uncommitted files is NOT deleted
- [x] Worktree younger than grace period is NOT deleted (even with --force-merged)
- [x] Worktree with open PR is NOT deleted
- [x] Truly merged PRs with dirty state ARE still cleaned up (existing behaviour preserved — safety checks only fire before the dirty check, not after)
- [x] ShellCheck passes on modified files (zero new violations)
- [x] Bash 3.2 compatible (no associative arrays, no bash 4+ features)

Closes #5694

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Enhanced safety for worktree cleanup operations to prevent accidental deletion of recently created branches, branches with open pull requests, and branches with uncommitted changes.

title: GH#5694: Fix worktree cleanup safety — grace period, open PR check, zero-ahead-dirty
body:
## Summary

- Add 3 safety checks to `cmd_clean()` in `worktree-helper.sh` to prevent deleting in-progress dirty worktrees that `git branch --merged` incorrectly considers merged
- Add `--grace-period=N` flag (default 4h) to skip recently-created worktrees
- Bash 3.2 compatible, ShellCheck clean (no new violations)

## Problem

`worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` (called by pulse) deletes dirty worktrees when a branch has 0 commits ahead of the default branch — `git branch --merged` treats it as merged, and `--force-merged` overrides the dirty check. A worktree created 5 seconds ago with uncommitted work gets destroyed.

## Safety Checks Added (GH#5694)

1. **Grace period** — worktrees younger than N hours (default 4, configurable via `--grace-period=N`) are skipped even with `--force-merged`
2. **Open PR check** — if a branch has an open PR on GitHub (`gh pr list --state open --head <branch>`), the worktree is active work and is skipped
3. **Zero-commits-ahead + dirty** — a branch with 0 commits ahead of default that has dirty files is in-progress work (just created, not yet committed), not completed merged work — skipped even with `--force-merged`

All three checks are applied in both the detection loop (display phase) and the removal loop (actual deletion phase) for consistency.
